prompt: Shield volcanoes such as those in Hawaii are very wide with gentle slopes, unlike steep cone volcanoes. The shape is mainly due to:

options.text: Wind spreading the ash evenly over a wide area
The volcano erupting only once, long ago
Very runny, low-viscosity lava that flows a long way before solidifying, building up broad layers
Ocean water flattening the lava as it erupts

explanation: Basaltic lava at shield volcanoes is fluid and flows far in thin sheets before hardening. Layer upon layer of these long flows builds a wide mountain with shallow slopes, like a warrior's shield lying on the ground.
